card.name: Just before adverse-reaction words
card.fires_on: Words that come right before adverse, toxicity or reaction terms, such as SER-IOUS, ocular, Serious and the Ad- of Adverse in CTCAE. It fires in drug-label safety sections.

modes.label: Start of Adverse Events
modes.description: The first piece of the word Adverse in the phrase Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events.
modes.example: a National Cancer Institute Common Terminology Criteria for<< Ad>>verse Events, version 5.

modes.label: Descriptor before toxicity
modes.description: A word like serious or ocular that modifies a following toxicity or adverse reaction term.

modes.label: Warning heading
modes.description: Part of the word SERIOUS in a boxed warning title ahead of TOXICITIES.
modes.example: WARNING: TREATMENT-RELATED MORTALITY AND SER<<IOUS>> TOXICITIES: INFECTIONS

card.writes: It pushes the model to predict adverse, complication, toxicity and toxic as the next word.
card.plain: It fires when the text is about to name an adverse reaction or toxicity.
